model_off.label: Model-disabled mock evaluation; not a real-model or sandbox run

sandbox_findings.claim: App token has payouts, disputes and reporting scopes
sandbox_findings.observed: The token carries payouts, disputes read, disputes update-seller, **disputes create** and reporting scopes. None was missing.

sandbox_findings.claim: Buyer can pay; tracking can be added and read back
sandbox_findings.observed: Three orders were captured ($400, $60, $25). The $400 capture: fee $14.45, net $385.55. `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED` arrived about 9 s after capture. Orders v2 `track` returned 201. `GET /v1/shipping/trackers` returned USPS, `SHIPPED`, `CARRIER_PROVIDED`.

sandbox_findings.claim: Single-item payout to a registered maker reaches SUCCESS
sandbox_findings.observed: The 201 create response carried **no item IDs** (F1). The batch went PENDING to SUCCESS in about 32 s. Webhooks were PROCESSING, then SUCCESS, each about 10 s after the change.

sandbox_findings.claim: Unregistered email gives UNCLAIMED reliably; unclaimed money is excluded from available
sandbox_findings.observed: All three items reached UNCLAIMED (`RECEIVER_UNREGISTERED`). Available dropped by $3.75 (3 × $1 plus a $0.25 fee each). Withheld did not change.

sandbox_findings.claim: Cancel works and GET shows RETURNED
sandbox_findings.observed: The cancel response (200) already shows `transaction_status: RETURNED`, and GET agrees. Cancelling again gives 400 `ITEM_ALREADY_CANCELLED`. Cancelling a SUCCESS item gives 400 `ITEM_INCORRECT_STATUS`. A `PAYMENT.PAYOUTS-ITEM.RETURNED` webhook arrived. The returned dollar showed in available within about 1.7 h.

sandbox_findings.claim: An identical replay is safe and resolves UNKNOWN; a duplicate `sender_batch_id` links to the original
sandbox_findings.observed: **Every** duplicate (exact replay, new request ID, changed body, losing concurrent POST) returned **400 `USER_BUSINESS_ERROR`** "Batch with given sender_batch_id already exists". The link to the original batch is in **`details[].link`** on host `api.sandbox.paypal.com`. A 50 ms-timeout lost response was resolved by following that link: one item, SUCCESS, $1, the same receiver. The harness recorded BLOCKED only because its link parser missed the nested link; batch `53YFFR9A9YFEA` was confirmed by hand.

sandbox_findings.claim: Payout negative-test values produce the documented errors
sandbox_findings.observed: All 14 values matched (batch PENDING, PROCESSING and DENIED; item CLOSED_MARKET, RECEIVER_UNREGISTERED, RISK_DECLINE; create and cancel errors).

sandbox_findings.claim: Disputes can be created (API or Resolution Center); PayPal holds the funds
sandbox_findings.observed: **API creation is BLOCKED**: 400 "No permissions to set target_client_id", even with the scope present. The Resolution Center route works. Disputes appeared in `GET /v1/customer/disputes` 190 to 256 s after the buyer submitted them, and `CUSTOMER.DISPUTE.CREATED` arrived about 4 s after creation. Disputes match captures through `disputed_transactions[].seller_transaction_id`. The $400 item-not-received dispute went **straight to UNDER_REVIEW / CHARGEBACK**; the $60 one to WAITING / INQUIRY, and the $25 one to WAITING / CHARGEBACK. **Hold:** `withheld_balance` never rose (0 of the expected $485 over 37 readings), but all three captures turned **PENDING**.

sandbox_findings.claim: Evidence can be submitted on an item-not-received dispute
sandbox_findings.observed: The $400 dispute (UNDER_REVIEW / CHARGEBACK) had only `provide_supporting_info` and `self` links: **no `provide_evidence`**. Evidence is possible only while WAITING_FOR_SELLER_RESPONSE **with** the link. On the $25 dispute, a multipart submission at that stage returned 200 (D10).

sandbox_findings.claim: Settlement works from UNDER_REVIEW; buyer close is a fallback
sandbox_findings.observed: **Adjudicate** SELLER_FAVOR (sandbox control, 200) gave `RESOLVED_SELLER_FAVOUR` / `INELIGIBLE_BUYER_PROTECTION_POLICY`. **Accept-claim** as JSON (200) gave `RESOLVED_BUYER_FAVOUR` / `SELLER_ISSUED_REFUND`, `amount_refunded` $60, plus a `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED` webhook. **Evidence** as multipart (200) at WAITING / CHARGEBACK moved the dispute to UNDER_REVIEW. **Buyer close** gave `CANCELED_BY_BUYER` / `BUYER_CANCELLED_CASE`.

sandbox_findings.claim: Webhooks verify through the API; deliveries can be late, duplicated or missing
sandbox_findings.observed: All 46 real deliveries verified `SUCCESS`. Median delay was 10.5 s (dispute events about 4 s). One outlier of about 2.7 days arrived while the catcher was offline. There was 1 duplicate, 1 out of order and 1 missing. `GET /v1/notifications/webhooks-events` works (47 listed, 2 never delivered to us), and resend works. **The simulator event also verified `SUCCESS`.**

sandbox_findings.claim: Balances can lag up to 3 h
sandbox_findings.observed: `last_refresh_time` and `as_of_time` lag by 1.4 to 2.4 h (median about 1.7 h), never over 3 h. available + withheld = total in all 585 readings. Payouts and returns appear in available within about 1.5 h. **No dispute event ever moved `withheld`**, and resolutions did not either. Transaction Search lag: BLOCKED (recorded, not chased).

sandbox_findings.claim: Agent Toolkit exposes only the allowlisted read tools
sandbox_findings.observed: With `paypal-agent-toolkit` 1.11.0 and langchain 0.3.23, the tool set is exactly `get_dispute`, `get_order_details`, `get_shipment_tracking`, `list_disputes`, `list_transactions`. Nothing unexpected, nothing missing.

sandbox_findings.claim: Disputed captures stay out of available.
sandbox_findings.observed: The three captures (Oct 23, 22:02 UTC) were disputed between 22:14 and 22:18. From then until the 07:29 refresh on Oct 24 (9.5 h, well past the 2.4 h maximum lag), available moved only by our payouts (5,000.00 to 4,988.75), and withheld stayed 0.00. The disputed money was frozen in the PENDING captures, not moved into withheld (D8, D12).

The rulings came at 12:19 on Oct 24, and available rose $383.07 at the 12:29 refresh. That is +$385.55 (the $400 capture's net, released by the seller-favour ruling) − $2.48 (the net effect of the $60 capture refunded in full through accept-claim). The $25 capture's dispute was still open, so it stayed out of available.

limitations: Mock and sandbox evidence are separate.
Zero measured invariant counts do not establish universal safety.
Disputes opened on captures already settled into available remain untested.
